strengths: The paper addresses a useful creative task: sketch colourisation controlled by region masks and palettes without task-specific training. Separating palette-conditioned global generation from local composition provides an understandable workflow, including previews and regeneration of intermediate images.

The evaluation covers animal faces, indoor/outdoor scenes, anime, and multi-object images. Table 1 reports improvements over all listed competitors on all five metrics for both Places365 subsets, and the best DCCW across all four local-colourisation datasets. Table 2 also shows consistent global FID improvements over the listed baselines.

Figures 9 and S7–S9 demonstrate visually appealing regional colour variations on hand-drawn sketches. The composite-to-final comparisons provide qualitative evidence that refinement can soften composition boundaries while retaining substantial sketch structure.

The manuscript includes useful investigations of palette size, attention injection, exceptional prompts, and the injection duration τ, plus qualitative comparisons with SDEdit and text-guided ControlNet. It also acknowledges reduced colour fidelity for small regions.
weaknesses: The main claim of precise regional colour control is not adequately isolated by the evaluation. DCCW measures palette similarity, but the manuscript does not clearly specify whether local results are evaluated separately within each requested mask. Whole-image palette similarity cannot establish correct spatial assignment. There are no explicit measurements of colour leakage, boundary quality, or preservation outside edited regions. Mapping arbitrary hexcodes to 147 CSS3 names also introduces quantisation before generation, so exact chromatic precision is stronger than the evidence supports.

The technical contribution beyond the cited composition and editing methods remains insufficiently established. The pipeline explicitly uses TF-ICON and Prompt-to-Prompt implementations, borrows exceptional prompts, and defines its attention operation with standard self-attention in Eq. 6. The stated custom mechanism mainly appears to concern the source of injected features and their temporal schedule. A controlled comparison against an existing composition pipeline using the same global images is missing; the small qualitative ablations do not establish how much improvement comes from the proposed local design.

The local composition specification contains a consequential error: M_tot = max(sum_i M_i, 1) removes the background even at pixels outside every mask. Although likely a correctable min/max typo, the intended implementation cannot follow this formula. Overlapping masks and summed transition masks can also produce values above one without a stated resolution rule. Moreover, bounding-box XOR regions need not be narrow boundary bands. These issues leave the claimed generality to arbitrary masks and mask counts unsupported.

The comparisons do not fully isolate the proposed contribution. Global evaluation lacks a quantitative Scribble ControlNet baseline with matched semantic and palette prompts. Local baselines receive reference patches, whereas the proposed system additionally uses explicit spatial masks; how equivalent location information is supplied to competitors is unclear. Consequently, the results establish useful system performance more convincingly than an advantage attributable to the composition mechanism.

Efficiency and reproducibility claims need stronger support. The advertised 15–20 steps do not account clearly for n+1 global generations, inversion, and subsequent refinement. No end-to-end latency, peak memory, or scaling with region count is reported. Attention injection layers, mask sampling, and intermediate-image selection during benchmark evaluation are also insufficiently specified.

Some conclusions contradict the tables: Section 4.2 claims the best local FID across all datasets, but ColorFlow achieves 94.87 on Danbooru versus 134.54 for the proposed method. The same discussion incorrectly describes higher DCCW as favourable. These are correctable reporting flaws, but the more material concerns about regional-control validation and contribution attribution currently outweigh the demonstrated practical merits.

strengths: The task is practically relevant: combining sketches, regional masks, and palettes offers useful control beyond text prompts. The two-stage workflow supports interactive inspection and regeneration without additional model training.

The evaluation covers animal faces, indoor/outdoor scenes, anime, and multi-object images. Table 1 reports the best local DCCW across all four evaluated settings and improvements across all five metrics for indoor/outdoor scenes. Table 2 also shows substantial global FID and perceptual improvements over several baselines.

The qualitative examples demonstrate appealing, spatially differentiated colourisation. Figures 10–11 and the supplementary SDEdit comparison provide useful evidence about attention injection, inversion, and the fidelity–harmonisation trade-off.
weaknesses: The central technical contribution is insufficiently isolated from existing composition machinery. The method explicitly adopts TF-ICON’s exceptional prompts and implementation, DPM-Solver++, and Prompt-to-Prompt, while Eq. 6 describes standard self-attention with a fixed injection schedule. There is no controlled quantitative comparison against the same global outputs composed using TF-ICON or a simpler refinement pipeline. The qualitative ablations support design choices but do not establish the added value of the claimed novel latent composition and custom attention mechanism.

Evidence for precise regional colour control is incomplete. Hexcodes are quantised to 147 CSS3 names and then realised through text-conditioned generation, so the input colours are only indirectly enforced. DCCW is relevant, but the manuscript does not specify whether local evaluation measures palettes separately within each requested mask. Whole-image palette agreement cannot establish correct spatial assignment. Boundary leakage, preservation outside edited regions, and performance on small regions are not quantified; the supplement explicitly acknowledges small-region colour loss.

The baseline protocol leaves attribution uncertain. The global quantitative comparison uses T2I-Adapter rather than a matched Scribble ControlNet baseline with the same automatically generated prompts. Figure S5 provides only qualitative ControlNet comparisons using a different prompting procedure. For local reference-based competitors, stating that identical patches are supplied does not sufficiently explain how multiple patches, their spatial correspondence, and method-specific controls are configured.

The efficiency claim conflates solver steps with complete pipeline cost. Section 3.2 generates n+1 global images before local inversion and refinement, with possible user regeneration. Reporting 15–20 steps without end-to-end latency, memory consumption, or scaling with region count does not substantiate the claimed fast interactive workflow.

There are consequential specification ambiguities, although some may be readily correctable. Section 3.3 defines M_tot = max(sum_i M_i, 1), which removes the background even outside every mask; the intended union presumably requires clipping from above. Summed transition masks can also exceed one when bounding rectangles overlap, making the stated noise blend invalid as a binary replacement. Overlap handling, mask sampling, and precise attention injection layers are insufficiently specified for reproduction.

Some performance conclusions contradict the tables. Section 4.2 claims the best local FID across all datasets, but ColorFlow achieves 94.87 on Danbooru versus 134.54 for the proposed method; the same paragraph incorrectly describes higher DCCW as favourable. These reporting errors alone would not determine rejection. Overall, the useful empirical results are outweighed by unresolved attribution of the technical advance and inadequate validation of the central precision and efficiency claims, supporting Weak Reject.

strengths: The paper addresses a useful problem: controlling sketch colourisation through region masks and palettes without task-specific fine-tuning. Separating global generation from local composition provides a practical workflow with opportunities for user inspection and refinement.

The evaluation spans animal faces, indoor/outdoor scenes, anime, and multi-object images. Table 1 reports improvements over all listed competitors on all five metrics for indoor and outdoor local colourisation, supporting the method’s usefulness beyond selected demonstrations.

Global colourisation results are also encouraging: Table 2 shows consistently strong FID and perceptual similarity relative to the evaluated baselines. Compatibility with an alternative anime-oriented backbone demonstrates useful modularity.

The qualitative examples illustrate flexible regional colour assignments and visibly smoother composites. Attention-injection, prompt, and blending-schedule ablations, together with the supplementary SDEdit comparison, provide some evidence for the design choices.
weaknesses: The principal claim of precise regional colour fidelity is only partially established. Hexcodes are quantised to 147 CSS3 names and then enforced through text-conditioned generation, so exact palette adherence is not guaranteed. The evaluation does not clearly specify whether DCCW is computed within each requested region, and lacks explicit measures of colour leakage, boundary preservation, or performance on small regions. Whole-image reconstruction metrics cannot establish these properties.

The methodological advance over existing composition techniques is insufficiently isolated. Exceptional prompts are attributed to TF-ICON, and the implementation builds on TF-ICON and Prompt-to-Prompt. Equation 6 specifies standard attention, with a temporal injection schedule rather than a clearly new attention operator. A matched comparison against existing composition machinery using the same generated inputs would clarify the contribution beyond a useful integration.

The central local-stage ablations are predominantly qualitative and use few examples. There is no aggregate comparison of the raw composite, refinement without noise replacement, refinement without attention injection, and the complete method. Consequently, the quantitative gains cannot be confidently attributed to the claimed local blending innovations.

Section 3.3 contains a consequential specification error: M_tot = max(sum_i M_i, 1) equals one outside every mask, eliminating the intended background contribution. This appears correctable, but the published equation does not implement the described operation. Overlapping masks also remain unresolved: summed image contributions and transition masks can exceed one. Moreover, a bounding-rectangle XOR is not generally a narrow boundary region and becomes empty for rectangular masks.

The efficiency claim lacks end-to-end evidence. The pipeline generates n+1 global images and then performs inversion and refinement; 15–20 solver steps therefore do not describe the complete computational cost. Runtime, peak memory, and scaling with region count are unreported. Exact attention-injection layers, mask-generation details, and sufficiently specific checkpoint/settings information are also missing for reliable reproduction.

Some conclusions overstate the reported evidence. Section 4.2 claims the best local FID across all datasets, but ColorFlow achieves 94.87 on Danbooru versus 134.54 for the proposed method; it also incorrectly describes higher DCCW as beneficial. These are correctable reporting issues. Overall, the broad empirical merits support a borderline recommendation, but uncertainty about the distinctive technical contribution and direct evidence for precise local control prevents a stronger acceptance recommendation.
